input.standard: ASTM E741 (single-zone concentration decay); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the volume of air served by scrubber-1-t3, as V = Qe * tau from the CO2 curve, with the occupant as source and the scrubber as pump.

monitoring.reason: FE-1 is the only occupant of the lab, the volume whose CO2 the test raises above its start value or holds high.

steps.why: Reduced effective flow (0.4 of 1 m3/min) so the lab CO2 moves towards a higher equilibrium than at full speed; hatch closed and held closed for the whole test. Record at 1 min.
Full speed, effective flow 1 m3/min: record the decay towards its equilibrium, about one time constant (first guess V=30 m3, tau=30 min) or more. Hatch unchanged.

abort.when: CO2 of the lab at or above 3200 ppm
the device refuses a step's command
FE-1 out of the 45-120 bpm band, monitoring lost, or one more person enters the lab

expected.start: Lab CO2 reads 1700 ppm at the start (measured), 1500 ppm below the 3200 abort and more than 200 ppm of headroom to it. One occupant awake produces about 0.38 L/min, i.e. about 12.7 ppm/min in a 30 m3 volume if unscrubbed.
expected.step1: At 40 percent the effective flow is about 0.4 m3/min and the equilibrium about G/Qe = 0.38/400 = 950 ppm above the scrubber-free baseline of the sensor. Since the start of 1700 ppm may already be above this equilibrium, the CO2 may drift down slowly (tau about 75 min for V=30 m3, over 15 min a change of only some tens of ppm) instead of rising. A rise would show a source larger than one occupant or an exchange through the closed hatch from hab-b (3 occupants). Either way, it stays under 2800 ppm.
expected.step2: At full speed the CO2 decays with tau = V/Qe = V/1 m3/min, about 30 min if V is 30 m3, towards an equilibrium near 380 ppm (0.38 L/min over 1000 L/min) plus any exchange; the scrubber lag (3.33 min) delays the start of the decay. The fit C(t)=Ceq+(C0-Ceq)exp(-t/tau) gives tau, then V_lab = 1 m3/min * tau, expected in the fitted range 10 to 200 m3, first guess 30 m3.
expected.refuted_if: The hypotheses fail if the fit residuals are systematic (not a single exponential: poor mixing or a leak), if the CO2 of hab-b moves with the lab's during the closed-hatch test (exchange through the hatch), if the occupant count changes, or if fitted tau differs by more than a factor of 2 between the two steps. If V is much above 60 m3 (tau over 60 min) the 40 min decay covers under one tau, and the fit is only an indication.

hypotheses: The lab is one well-mixed zone.

The hatch is held closed in both steps; the exchange through the closed hatch to hab-b is not measured and is not assumed to be zero (designed inter-module ventilation with the hatch closed: 3 m3/min per station-topology); the CO2 of hab-b is recorded to show it.
The source is one occupant (FE-1) awake at about 0.38 L/min (0.26 to 0.45), held constant; nobody enters or leaves the lab.
The effective flow is Qe = 1 m3/min at full speed and scales with speed, and the lag is 3.33 min (scrubber-1 datasheet).
At 40 percent speed the lab may not rise above its 1700 ppm start; the test then relies on the decay curves, not on a rise.
Records: lab CO2 every minute, hab-b CO2 every minute, scrubber speed commands and whether they were accepted.
